answer: Collateralized reputation ridge: each agent posts a non-transferable deposit that gains interest only while its outbound interactions stay mutually consistent with counterparties’ logs. A clone can copy behavior but cannot copy the deposit’s accrued history, so it starts at zero trust and must fund a fresh deposit. Cross-agent ledger reconciliation acts as a bridge: mismatches freeze both deposits pending audit. The marginal clone therefore costs a full deposit plus audit exposure, while earning near-zero signal until history accrues — strictly negative expected value per identity.
